name: e-HKD / e-HKD+
application_scope: Domestic payments and settlement; specific cross-border use cases must be checked in individual reports
note: e-HKD+ also studies tokenised deposits, which are a separate type of money. Do not equate completion of the retail pilot with public retail issuance.

name: Inthanon-LionRock / Project mBridge
jurisdiction: Hong Kong participation in a multi-jurisdiction project
lead_authority: Participating central banks and monetary authorities; BIS Innovation Hub historical collaboration
currency: Multiple participating currencies; consult the dated report for the specific transaction set
application_scope: Cross-border payments, foreign exchange and payment-versus-payment settlement
note: Observers are not full participants. BIS project status Concluded describes BIS involvement and must not be used to assert that all partner operations ceased.

name: Project Ensemble / EnsembleTX
jurisdiction: Hong Kong; individual international collaborations tagged in source documents
currency: HKD settlement context; tokenised Central Bank Money and tokenised deposits must remain distinct
application_scope: Interbank settlement of tokenised deposits and tokenised asset transactions
note: Keep 2024 experimentation, 2025 RTGS-based pilot, and 2026 tokenised CeBM settlement milestones separate.

name: Project Aurum / Aurum Phase 2
lead_authority: BIS Innovation Hub Hong Kong Centre in collaboration with HKMA and research partners
currency: Experimental digital cash architecture; no issued currency inferred
application_scope: Two-tier prototype, privacy-enhancing technologies and compliance research
note: International collaboration does not by itself make this a live cross-border payment system. CBDC-backed stablecoin experiments are not the Hong Kong licensed stablecoin regime.

name: Project Sela
jurisdiction: Hong Kong and Israel research collaboration
lead_authority: BIS Innovation Hub, HKMA and Bank of Israel
currency: Experimental retail CBDC; no issued currency inferred
application_scope: Access, intermediary roles and cyber security
note: A cross-jurisdiction research collaboration, not evidence of an operational Hong Kong-Israel payment corridor.

name: Cross-boundary e-CNY pilot in Hong Kong
lead_authority: PBoC and HKMA cross-boundary collaboration; e-CNY is not issued by HKMA
application_scope: Wallet access, FPS top-ups and Mainland merchant payments for Hong Kong residents
note: Usage limits and participating bank counts belong to the dated announcement, not an automatically current product specification.
